04/11/2026.report: After being crossed by WINNING DIAMOND approaching the 1300 Metres commenced to race keenly and was steadied to avoid WINNING DIAMOND. When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to hold a handy position with cover. She said in the early stages LOVELY MILES showed sufficient pace to hold a position behind the leader WINNING DIAMOND. She said approaching the 1100 Metres when her mount was racing keenly she was reluctant to make use of it to prevent SUPER SICARIO from shifting in as she was concerned this would result in her mount racing too keenly. She said as a result SUPER SICARIO was able to obtain a position in advance of LOVELY MILES and behind WINNING DIAMOND near the 1100 Metres. When questioned as the reason why her mount was obliged to race wide and without cover from the 1000 Metres, Apprentice Yuen stated that when making the turn near the 1000 Metres her mount shifted out which provided an opportunity for GOR GOR to obtain a position one-off behind SUPER SICARIO and this resulted in her mount being obliged to race wide and without cover thereafter. She further stated that after making contact with GOR GOR near the 550 Metres her mount shifted out which resulted in TELECOM POWER then improving to her inside and LOVELY MILES being obliged to race very wide making the Home Turn. Trainer P F Yiu confirmed the instructions were consistent with previous instructions he issued at the horse’s most recent starts. The Stewards advised Apprentice Yuen that she had made two errors of judgement in the early stages firstly near the 1100 Metres by not making a greater effort to hold her position behind WINNING DIAMOND to prevent SUPER SICARIO from shifting in and secondly near the 1000 Metres by permitting her mount to shift out to a three wide position which afforded GOR GOR the opportunity to obtain a position one-off following SUPER SICARIO. She was further advised that whilst acknowledging her inexperience as an apprentice jockey in future she would be expected to show better judgement than what she did during the early stages of this race. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to have sustained a laceration to the right hind cannon.
04/11/2026.quote: A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to have sustained a laceration to the right hind cannon.

06/04/2025.report: Withdrawn on raceday morning by order of the Stewards (inadvertent treatment). An inquiry into the matter was adjourned to a date to be fixed to allow Trainer W K Mo to attend who was not currently present in Hong Kong. Before being allowed to race again, LEGENDARY IMPACT will be subjected to an official veterinary examination. <9/4/2025 Adjourned Inquiry – 6 April 2025 Sha Tin Racemeeting – Race 6 (567)> The Stewards today conducted an inquiry into the withdrawal of LEGENDARY IMPACT from the said race. Evidence was taken from Trainer W K Mo, Assistant Trainer K H Lam, Work Riders S L Lee and C K Sze, and Dr B S Forbes, Head of Veterinary Regulation, Welfare and Biosecurity Policy. After considering all the evidence, the Stewards established that despite having systems in place to prevent the administration of treatment on raceday, subsequent to LEGENDARY IMPACT working on the morning of 6 April 2025, it was inadvertently treated with Swede Clay, a topical treatment which does not contain any prohibited substances and is the usual treatment for the horse post track work. The Stewards were satisfied that the treatment was an oversight and not intentional conduct. Mr Mo pleaded guilty to a charge under Rule 155(29) for causing the application of the raceday treatment in that he did not have proper processes in place to prevent such treatment occurring. Mr Mo was fined the sum of $20,000. A report will be made to the Stables Management in relation to the conduct of the above staff members.

21/10/2026.report: Shifted in at the start and was bumped. The Stewards considered a protest/objection lodged by Mr D Eustace, trainer of the 3rd placegetter, MASTER PHOENIX, against FLYING TING LOK (Apprentice P N Wong) being declared the 2nd placegetter alleging interference on the Home Turn. After taking evidence from the parties concerned the Stewards found that FLYING TING LOK shifted out near the 350 Metres when not sufficiently clear of MASTER PHOENIX, resulting in MASTER PHOENIX being checked to avoid FLYING TING LOK, shifting out and losing ground. The Stewards were satisfied that had this incident not have occurred MASTER PHOENIX would have finished in advance of FLYING TING LOK. Therefore the protest/objection was sustained and the placings amended to read No. 4, VIRTUS GLORY, 1st; No. 7, MASTER PHOENIX, 2nd; No. 8, FLYING TING LOK, 3rd; and No. 2, MASTER RESOLUTE, 4th. At a subsequent inquiry Apprentice P N Wong pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that near the 350 Metres she allowed her mount to shift out when insufficiently clear of MASTER PHOENIX, resulting in MASTER PHOENIX being taken out and having to be checked to avoid FLYING TING LOK. Apprentice Wong was suspended from riding in races for a period to commence on Sunday, 22 November 2026 and to expire on Thursday, 26 November 2026 on which day she may resume race riding (2 Hong Kong racedays). In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered her good race riding record. Sent for sampling post-race.

25/10/2026.report: When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and lead if circumstances permitted. She said in accordance with her instructions she rode her mount along in the early stages, however, AWESOME FLUKE took some time to muster speed which resulted in a number of runners crossing her mount in the early stages. She said when left without cover near the 1400 Metres AWESOME FLUKE then commenced to race keenly and her intention was to endeavour to obtain a position with cover behind DEFINITIVE. She said when CALIFORNIATOTALITY maintained its position one-off behind DEFINITIVE, this resulted in AWESOME FLUKE being obliged to race wide and without cover. When questioned if there was an opportunity to go forward from the 1300 Metres having regard to the early stages being run outside of standard time, Apprentice Yuen agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect she had made an error of judgement in not allowing her mount to stride forward, particularly as it was racing keenly. She added that when positioned to the outside of DEFINITIVE she was mindful not to crowd runners to her inside and for this reason she remained racing three wide and without cover from the 900 Metres and into the Home Straight. Trainer P F Yiu confirmed the instructions were to go forward and agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect Apprentice Yuen should have taken the initiative to go forward and cross DEFINITIVE. When questioned regarding the tactics adopted on the stablemate CHILL EASY, Mr Yiu advised that he had expected the horse to hold a midfield position and was surprised that AWESOME FLUKE remained three deep during the race, particularly from barrier 6 having regard to the instructions. He said it was not the intention of the stable for this to occur and in the circumstances it was Apprentice Yuen’s riding which led to CHILL EASY being able to obtain cover behind AWESOME FLUKE.

She said when left without cover near the 1400 Metres AWESOME FLUKE then commenced to race keenly and her intention was to endeavour to obtain a position with cover behind DEFINITIVE. She said when CALIFORNIATOTALITY maintained its position one-off behind DEFINITIVE, this resulted in AWESOME FLUKE being obliged to race wide and without cover. When questioned if there was an opportunity to go forward from the 1300 Metres having regard to the early stages being run outside of standard time, Apprentice Yuen agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect she had made an error of judgement in not allowing her mount to stride forward, particularly as it was racing keenly. She added that when positioned to the outside of DEFINITIVE she was mindful not to crowd runners to her inside and for this reason she remained racing three wide and without cover from the 900 Metres and into the Home Straight. Trainer P F Yiu confirmed the instructions were to go forward and agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect Apprentice Yuen should have taken the initiative to go forward and cross DEFINITIVE. When questioned regarding the tactics adopted on the stablemate CHILL EASY, Mr Yiu advised that he had expected the horse to hold a midfield position and was surprised that AWESOME FLUKE remained three deep during the race, particularly from barrier 6 having regard to the instructions. He said it was not the intention of the stable for this to occur and in the circumstances it was Apprentice Yuen’s riding which led to CHILL EASY being able to obtain cover behind AWESOME FLUKE.
